title: osf-2003-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Kimbusa

won.source: OSF's own Title History page: 'March 23, 2002, Sunday Night Slam, Jane Reagan makes International Title the new OSF World Title, and names then-International champ Kimbusa as the first OSF titleholder.' The page's year reads 2002; its front page of 1 April 2003 says the champion was crowned 'on last Slam', and 23 March was a Sunday in 2003, not 2002.

note: Still listed as champion on the Champions page captured 16 April 2003, with Tempest, Fatico and Ray Chavez as the ranked contenders.

title: osf-2003-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Tempest

won.source: No page records the night. The Champions page of 16 April 2003 lists Kimbusa as champion with Tempest first contender; OSF's Fighter Spotlight of 12 May 2003 speaks of 'a shot at Tempest and the OSF Title'.

note: Defended against Akage Kitagami on the 4 June 2003 Assault with Inphino Blitz as special referee; her own column of 2 June calls her 'the OSF world champion just now'. The 16 July news announces Tempest against Inphino Blitz for the championship; the result is not captured.

title: osf-2003-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Inphino Blitz

won.source: No page records the night. OSF's president calls him the World Champion in columns of 7 and 14 October 2003, and the B3 review has him defending the title against Kenyatta Jackson; the last dated mention of Tempest as champion is 16 July 2003.

note: Defended against Kenyatta Jackson at B3 and retained with the Inphinite kick.
